# Configure the MCP Sidecar

This page describes how to configure the MCP Sidecar on Kubernetes. You register AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers so that agent tool calls travel through the sidecar. To learn how the sidecar governs tool calls, refer to [Govern tool access with the MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Workflow

Complete the following steps:

1. Register AI agents.
1. Register MCP servers.
1. Connect agents to MCP servers.
1. Send tool calls through the sidecar.
1. Configure human approval.
1. Verify the configuration.

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with the [`ai.agent.image`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-agent-image) Helm value set. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
- An AI agent that uses an MCP client.
- One or more MCP servers that use a supported transport. In-mesh servers run in the service mesh. External servers need a terminating gateway.

## Register AI agents

Annotate the pod template of each AI agent with the `ai-agent` role. Consul injects the MCP Sidecar into the pod.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: ai-agent
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The sidecar uses the defaults in the [`AgentConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/agentconfig) resource. Use the annotations to override a default for one pod. Each port must not conflict with the application port or the Envoy proxy port, `20000`.

| Setting | Purpose | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MCP connectivity port | The loopback port the agent sends tool calls to, at `/mcp` | `15101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-mcp-port` |
| Agent interceptor port | The loopback port of the MCP Sidecar interceptor | `21101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-interceptor-port` |
| Human approval server port | The loopback port that receives approval requests | `16101` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-port` |
| Human approval timeout | How long the interceptor waits for a verdict before it rejects the call | `60s` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-approval-timeout` |

The sidecar listens on a Unix domain socket by default. In local development, or where a shared socket volume is unavailable, set `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-addr` to switch the listener to TCP. Refer to [Kubernetes annotations and labels](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/annotation-label) for details.

## Register MCP servers

Annotate the pod template of each in-mesh MCP server with the `mcp-server` role. Consul registers the service with the `mcp-server` role and adds an MCP router filter to the pod's inbound Envoy listener.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="5">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: mcp-server
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The registration uses the defaults in the [`McpServerConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/mcpserverconfig) resource. Use the annotations to override a default for one pod.

| Setting | Default | Annotation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP transport | `streamable-http` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-transport` |
| MCP path | `/mcp` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-path` |
| MCP protocol version | `2025-03-26` | `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-mcp-server-protocol-version` |

The `McpServerConfig` resource also sets `interceptorPort`, the TCP port the MCP server container listens on inside the pod. It defaults to `21102`.

## Connect agents to MCP servers

1. Add each MCP server as an explicit upstream of the agent. Consul also uses the agent's explicit upstreams to decide the audiences for on-behalf-of token exchange.

   ```yaml
   template:
     metadata:
       annotations:
         consul.hashicorp.com/connect-service-upstreams: "<mcp-server>:<local-port>"
   ```

   <!-- TODO: Confirm how the explicit upstream relates to the MCP listener on port 15101. Does the agent call the upstream's local port, or only localhost:15101/mcp with the listener selecting the server? -->

1. Allow the agent to call each MCP server with a service intention.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="mcp-intentions.yaml">

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
   kind: ServiceIntentions
   metadata:
     name: <mcp-server>
   spec:
     destination:
       name: <mcp-server>
     sources:
       - name: <agent-service>
         action: allow
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

   ```shell-session
   $ kubectl apply --filename mcp-intentions.yaml
   ```

To reach an MCP server outside the mesh, route the call through a terminating gateway. Refer to [Configure external credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection/configure). To carry the user's identity to the MCP server, refer to [Configure OAuth clients for AI agents and MCP servers](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity/configure-oauth-clients).

## Send tool calls through the sidecar

Configure the agent's MCP client to send requests to the MCP listener on loopback:

```plaintext
http://localhost:15101/mcp
```

If you changed the MCP connectivity port, use that port instead.

## Configure human approval

The interceptor sends an approval request for each protected tool to the approval server on port `16101` and waits for a verdict. If no verdict arrives before the approval timeout, the interceptor rejects the call.

To change the timeout for every agent, set `spec.defaults.hitl.approvalTimeout` in the `AgentConfig` resource. To change it for one pod, set the `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-hitl-approval-timeout` annotation.

## Verify the configuration

1. Send a tool discovery request from the agent to `localhost:15101/mcp`, and confirm that the response lists the tools the agent is allowed to see.
1. Call a tool, and confirm that the MCP server receives the request.
1. Call a protected tool without approving it, and confirm that the sidecar rejects the call after the approval timeout.
